title: LEAF: An Adaptation Framework against Noisy Data on Edge through Ultra Low-Cost Training
problem: Machine learning models deployed on edge devices experience performance degradation from input noise and time-varying conditions. Continual re-training is needed to adapt, but edge devices lack the computational resources to perform this expensive training.
motivation: Enabling energy-efficient continual learning on resource-constrained edge devices is critical for real-world computer vision applications that must adapt to noisy, degraded input data.
method: LEAF works by studying how machine learning models (specifically convolutional neural networks or CNNs) behave when they see degraded, noisy images. It uses two complementary strategies to make training require less computation. First, it implements selective experience replay (SER)—during training, it skips over unimportant or redundant images, reducing the amount of computation needed for both forward and backward passes (the two main computational steps in training). Second, it uses pseudo noise dithering (PND) to compress the gradients (the values that guide weight updates) down to just 3 or 4 bits per number instead of full precision, which lets the model use mostly integer arithmetic (faster computation) instead of expensive floating-point math during gradient updates.
key_novelty: LEAF combines selective experience replay (using only important training examples) and pseudo noise dithering (compressing the gradient values—the adjustments made during training—to just 3 or 4 bits) to enable low-cost retraining on noisy degraded images while maintaining accuracy.
contributions: Selective experience replay technique to skip unimportant images and reduce training cost
Pseudo noise dithering method for extreme quantization of error gradients
Integrated LEAF framework demonstrating 3.64-8.40× speedup in forward/backward processing
Evaluation showing <0.5% accuracy loss across multiple architectures and degradation types
primary_theme: ultra-low-cost CNN adaptation for noisy edge deployment
